senses.gloss:
ITA-5.75.22 kṣud-vegarodhaḥ क्षुद्-वेगरोधः
Disorder due to suppression of hunger
A disorder characterized by some or all the following signs and symptoms: emaciation; weakness; discoloration; generalized body aches; loss of taste; giddiness or dizziness; drowsiness/lassitude; diminished vision; breaking type of pain in body; fatigued mind and body; pain.

ITA-5.62.1 kṣudrarogaḥ क्षुद्ररोगः
Group of disorders in which dosha pathogenesis has a single definitive diagnostic outcome
Miscellaneous group of morbid conditions ranging from very fatal conditions such as agnirōhiṇī and valmīka to conditions occurring in children such as ajagallikā and ahipūtanā These conditions have a specific, consolidated description of presenting signs and symptoms and minimum details in respect of etiology, subtypes, etc., compared with major disorders such as jvara, prameha and kuṣṭa.

ITA-5.20.6 kṣudraśvāsaḥ क्षुद्रश्वासः
Mild dyspnoea
A disorder characterized by some or all the following signs and symptoms: not very troublesome breathing; not harmful for the body; not distressing; not hampering intake of food or liquids; not painful for sense organs; not causing emergencies.

IT.3.11.36 kṣudrāntrāvayavaḥ क्षुद्रान्त्रावयवः
Small intestinal loops

ITA-5.19.4 kṣudrāhikkā क्षुद्राहिक्का
Mild or insignificant hiccups
A disorder characterized by hiccups increasing with exertion and decreasing after food intake; long interval; feeble bouts at long intervals; starting from jatrumūla and ending at jatrumūla.

ITA-9.1.47 kṣudhā क्षुधा
Therapeutic sustained hunger
The process of keeping a person hungry as a therapeutic measure.

ITA-9.2.61 kṣudhā क्षुधा
Sweating induced by hunger
A type of sudation therapy in which diaphoresis is achieved by not attending to hunger pangs.

ITA-5.76.145 kṣudhārtasya nasya vyāpadaḥ क्षुधार्तस्य नस्य व्यापदः
Condition due to inhalation therapy administered to person who is hungry
A condition characterized by clinical features of vāta prakopa.

ITA-5.35.11 kṣunnirodhaja-udāvartaḥ क्षुन्निरोधज-उदावर्तः
Disorders of reversed or altered visceral movement due to suppression of hunger
A disorder characterized by some or all the following signs and symptoms: drowsiness/lassitude; generalized body aches; loss of taste; dizziness/confusion; diminished vision; exhaustion/fatigue.
